title: Inside Ogun State’s Biggest Founders Meetup: This Month It’s All About Revenue
excerpt: Founders Friday Abeokuta is back for its June edition, bringing together entrepreneurs, startup founders, and ecosystem players for an evening focused on one of the most practical questions in business: how do you actually make money consistently?
body:
A lot of founders can build a product. Fewer can build a business that generates revenue reliably. That gap is what Founders Friday Abeokuta is putting at the center of its June edition, themed “Understanding Revenue Models.”

The event, hosted in partnership with Jekacode Hub, brings together entrepreneurs, business owners, innovators, and ecosystem leaders for an evening of conversations, pitches, and community. It is one of the more consistent gathering points for founders in Ogun State, and this edition is shaping up to be one of its more practical ones.

The programme is built around the idea that having a good product is only part of the equation. What trips most early-stage founders is figuring out how that product makes money consistently, how to price it right, how to communicate its value, and how to build growth systems that hold up beyond the initial excitement of launching. Experienced entrepreneurs and industry professionals will share insights from their own journeys across technology, product development, and business growth.

A Founder Pitch Session is also on the agenda, with five selected businesses presenting their models to the room for direct community feedback. The format is designed to give founders clarity and challenge assumptions in a room that’s invested in seeing them succeed rather than just evaluate them.

The June edition also includes a Business Owners Appreciation Program, distributing N140,000 in cash support among seven business owners, alongside discount vouchers from community service providers and free 30-minute advisory sessions with experienced experts. It is a practical gesture toward the reality that many founders are building through real financial pressure, not just ideation challenges.

For anyone building in Ogun State’s tech and startup ecosystem, this is the kind of room worth being in. The combination of structured learning, live pitching, and direct peer community makes Founders Friday one of the more grounded ecosystem events on the calendar.

The June edition holds on Friday, June 26th at 4:00 PM at Jekacode Hub, Casa Bella, No. 40 Abiola Way, Abeokuta. Registration is open.

title: How Ogun State Is Building One of Nigeria’s Fastest-Growing Technology Ecosystems
excerpt: From expanding startup networks and digital skills programmes to AI adoption and emerging local startups, Ogun State is steadily building a technology ecosystem that is positioning itself as one of Nigeria’s most active innovation hubs outside Lagos.
body:
Ogun State's technology ecosystem is steadily becoming one of the most active innovation communities in southwestern Nigeria. Across the state, startup founders, digital hubs, training programmes, and technology communities are building solutions and creating opportunities that are giving Ogun a stronger place in Nigeria's tech conversation.

One sign of this growth is the expanding network of support for builders. Ogun Tech Community says it now connects more than 50 hubs, coworking spaces, startups, and skill development organisations across the state. This growing network is helping founders and creators find resources and collaborate without leaving Ogun.

The state is also preparing for Ogun Digital Summit 2026, an event designed to bring together founders, creators, and technology talent in Abeokuta. The summit is expected to give local startups more visibility and create opportunities for partnerships and knowledge sharing.

Infrastructure and talent development are also receiving attention. Ogun Tech Hub continues to be promoted as a technology park project built through public private partnership, while the state has produced certified digital technician trainees through a skills programme focused on strengthening technical support capacity.

Beyond training and infrastructure, technology is increasingly being applied to solve real problems. Local partnerships have introduced artificial intelligence ideas aimed at improving government efficiency and transparency, while state officials have promoted AI driven platforms for education, spatial data, and farmer information management.

There is also growing confidence among local stakeholders who now describe Ogun as one of Nigeria's most promising emerging startup regions. Their message to founders is simple: build here and stay here.

Recent ecosystem roundups have highlighted startups such as EduTAMS, Farmspeaks, Vant, and Frootify as examples of local companies making visible progress. Together, these developments suggest that Ogun is not just talking about innovation. It is steadily building an ecosystem that could become one of Nigeria's strongest technology communities outside Lagos.

title: Ogun State’s Vant Backs Nigeria’s Next Generation of Tech Talent Through Smartan House Partnership
excerpt: Vant, the African business infrastructure startup from Ogun State, has been appointed a Smartan House Champion, committing to open doors for high-potential young Nigerians being trained on real-world work inside one of Lagos’s most quietly remarkable youth development programmes.
body:
It started with a phone call from Johnson Abbaly. By the time Paul and Raph from Vant walked out of Smartan House, something had shifted.

Smartan House is a social enterprise and residential programme that finds high-potential young Nigerians, including teenagers from underprivileged communities, and places them inside real work environments. Not simulations. Not classroom exercises. Live briefs, actual deliverables, and professional standards that most adults would find demanding. Graduates have won full scholarships to institutions like the African Leadership Academy, secured internships with major organisations, and earned hundreds of thousands of naira from project work while still in their teens.

Abbaly, the programme’s founder and president, has spent years doing something most people only talk about: finding overlooked young Nigerians and giving them access to serious mentorship, high-skill work, and a community that treats their potential as real rather than theoretical.

When the Vant team arrived, what they found wasn’t what most people picture when they hear “youth programme.” The room had sharpness to it. Curiosity. Young people actively working through real problems for real organisations. The kind of energy that tends to settle something in you rather than inspire you temporarily.

At the end of the visit, Vant was formally appointed as a Smartan House Champion, a commitment, not a ceremonial title, to actively support the mission of developing the next generation of African talent. For Vant, a startup building business infrastructure and financial tools for African merchants and operators, the partnership isn’t a detour from its core mission. It’s an extension of it.

Vant was built around a belief that African businesses deserve world-class operational tools regardless of where they’re located or how big they are. That belief, the team says, extends beyond today’s merchants to the teenager currently solving a live brief inside Smartan House who will one day be a founder, an operator, or an employer. Investing in that person now is part of the same story.

For Ogun State’s ecosystem, the partnership is worth noting. It’s a signal that startups building out of the state are not only shipping products but also showing up in the broader Nigerian tech and talent conversation, backing programmes, building relationships, and taking a longer view of what ecosystem participation actually looks like.

title: Vant Joins FirstFounders Portfolio as It Scales Financial OS for African SMEs
excerpt: Vant, the Ogun State fintech building a financial operating system for African small businesses, has been accepted into FirstFounders, an AI-first venture studio backing high-growth African startups across fintech, consumer, and entertainment.
body:
Vant has a new backer. The Ogun State startup has joined the portfolio of FirstFounders, an AI-first venture studio focused on Africa’s next generation of high-growth companies. The studio backs startups across fintech, consumer, and entertainment, and its decision to bring Vant in signals confidence in both the team and the problem they’re building around.

The problem is a real one. African small and medium businesses have long operated without the kind of financial infrastructure that businesses in more developed markets take for granted. Banking, payments, storefronts, trade financing, and logistics typically sit across five different tools, none of which talk to each other cleanly. Vant is building one platform to bring all of that together, what the team describes as a financial operating system for African SMEs.

The traction behind that vision is already visible. Vant has processed over 89,000 transactions across four countries and built partnerships with Stripe, Interswitch, JICA, MIT Solve, and WIPO. That last name is particularly notable given the startup’s recent selection as a top 12 finalist in WIPO’s IP Labs 2.0 programme, a recognition that came from a pool of over 700 global applicants.

The FirstFounders partnership brings more than capital. For a startup at Vant’s stage, venture studio support means access to infrastructure, networks, and operational expertise that can meaningfully accelerate the build. Joining alongside other founders working on closing the gap between African ambition and global infrastructure gives the team a community that understands the specific challenge they’re navigating.

For Ogun State’s ecosystem, this is another marker worth paying attention to. Vant is now a WIPO-recognised, venture-backed fintech with cross-border transaction volume and partnerships spanning global payment rails. That’s a profile that would stand out in any ecosystem, and it’s being built out of Ogun State.

title: Ogun State’s Vant Makes Global Top 12 in WIPO’s IP Labs 2.0 Competition
excerpt: Vant, the Ogun State business infrastructure startup, has been selected as one of 12 finalists from over 700 applicants worldwide in the World Intellectual Property Organization’s IP Labs 2.0 programme, earning a spot to present at the United Nations House in Abuja.
body:
Out of more than 700 startups and innovators from across the world, Vant made the cut. The Ogun State based startup has been named one of the top 12 finalists in IP Labs 2.0, a global innovation programme powered by the World Intellectual Property Organization, the UN agency responsible for intellectual property policy and global innovation frameworks.

The selection puts Vant in rare company. IP Labs 2.0 drew applications from startups across multiple continents, and being shortlisted to 12 from that pool is a meaningful signal that what the team is building has caught attention well beyond Nigeria’s borders.

As part of the recognition, Vant has been invited to present at the United Nations House in Abuja, a venue that carries weight not just symbolically but practically, connecting finalists with global policymakers, development partners, and fellow innovators working on problems at a similar scale of ambition.

The milestone was shared by Oluwafisayomi Adesanya on behalf of the Vant team, framing the selection as validation of the direction the company has been heading rather than a destination in itself.

For Vant, which is building business infrastructure and financial tools designed to give African merchants and operators access to the kind of operational systems that have historically been out of reach, the WIPO recognition adds a layer of credibility that matters when you’re trying to build trust with the businesses you serve.

It also adds another data point to a story that has been developing quietly out of Ogun State. In a short period, Vant has moved from building product to earning recognition from one of the world’s most respected international bodies on innovation. That kind of trajectory doesn’t happen by accident, and it puts the startup firmly on the list of Ogun State companies worth watching closely.

title: What Nigeria’s New Data Localisation Rule Means for Ogun State’s Fintech Builders
excerpt: The Central Bank of Nigeria has given banks and fintechs six months to start storing Nigerian payment data on local servers. Here’s what that means for fintech founders building out of Ogun State.
body:
Nigeria’s fintech sector just got a new compliance deadline, and it’s one that touches anyone handling payment data, regardless of how big or small the company is.

The Central Bank of Nigeria has directed banks, fintechs, mobile money operators, and other payment service providers to store all payment transaction data generated within Nigeria on local servers. The directive, signed by Rakiya Yusuf, the CBN’s Director of Payments System Supervision, gives operators until January 1, 2027 to comply. It comes packaged with broader rules around market structure, ultimate beneficial ownership disclosure, and systemic oversight for payment system participants.

The core ask is straightforward. Any entity processing payments in Nigeria has to keep that data within the country, in line with Nigerian data protection law. The CBN says the goal is better regulatory visibility, stronger consumer protection, and lower risk from offshore data storage.

For fintechs that currently rely on foreign cloud infrastructure or cross-border data processing, this isn’t a small adjustment. It means evaluating where data currently lives, what it would take to migrate to local infrastructure, and whether that infrastructure can actually handle the load reliably. Reports following the announcement note that fintech executives are already raising concerns about local data center readiness and the cost of migration.

This matters for Ogun State’s fintech builders for a simple reason: the state has a growing cluster of founders working in payments, lending, and financial tools, and compliance rules like this apply the same way whether a company is operating out of Lagos or building from Ogun State. A six month runway sounds generous until you factor in vendor selection, testing, and the operational risk of moving live financial data without downtime.

There’s also a quieter opportunity buried in this directive. As fintechs across the country look for local infrastructure providers and compliance support, that creates demand fintech-adjacent service providers and infrastructure startups could step into, including ones built closer to Lagos than to Abuja. For Ogun State’s ecosystem, the question worth tracking is whether any local players position themselves to meet that need rather than just absorb the compliance cost.

The CBN’s broader push also includes new disclosure rules requiring payment operators to reveal who actually owns and controls their companies, even where ownership is layered through multiple entities. Combined with the data localisation rule, it signals a regulator tightening its grip on a sector that has scaled fast and, until now, operated with relatively loose oversight.

For Ogun State founders building in fintech, the deadline is one to put on the calendar early. January 2027 is not far off once infrastructure planning is factored in.

title: TickiSpot Wants to Fix the Mess Behind Event Planning in Nigeria
excerpt: TickiSpot is building an all-in-one event management and ticketing platform for African organizers from Ogun State, combining ticket sales, live streaming, real-time chat, and analytics into one dashboard.
body:
Anyone who has organized an event in Nigeria knows the drill. Ticket sales on one app, attendee tracking on a spreadsheet, payment confirmations scattered across bank alerts, and audience engagement left to WhatsApp groups nobody checks consistently. TickiSpot, built by a team based in Ogun State, was shaped around that exact frustration.

The platform gives organizers a single dashboard to create events, sell tickets online, livestream sessions, manage attendees, and engage their audience in real time. For attendees, it is solving a different problem: event discovery that currently feels scattered, with little consistency in how people find out what is happening or where.

Built on the MERN stack, TickiSpot combines ticketing, live streaming, real-time chat, and analytics into one system. The goal is straightforward: organizers stop juggling five different tools, and attendees get an experience that feels connected instead of patched together from separate apps.

The timing lines up with where the global events industry is heading. The sector is valued at over $1.45 trillion today and projected to reach $2.1 trillion by 2032, with the event tech segment alone expected to grow from $18.4 billion to over $55 billion in that window. More than 67% of organizers are already shifting toward hybrid and virtual formats, which is precisely the space TickiSpot is positioning itself in.

For now, the more immediate opportunity is local. Nigeria’s event tech space is still fragmented, without a dominant platform handling the full journey from organizer to attendee. That gives a team building from Ogun State room to establish traction before any plan to expand beyond Nigeria’s borders.

TickiSpot is currently at MVP stage. Event creation, the ticketing system, and the organizer dashboard are already built. Payment integration, live streaming, mobile optimization, and advanced analytics are next in line for development.

The team behind TickiSpot describes it as more than a ticketing tool, framing it instead as a full event ecosystem meant to help organizers increase revenue while giving attendees a smoother path from discovery to attendance. It is also one more example of Ogun State based founders building products with ambitions well beyond the state.

title: Trova: How an Ogun State Startup is Building a More Meaningful Dating Experience Beyond Endless Swiping
excerpt: Trova is a relationship focused platform on a mission to make online dating more intentional, helping people build genuine connections through shared interests, compatibility, and authentic interactions.
body:
In an era where digital platforms have made communication easier than ever, many people still struggle to form meaningful relationships online. While dating apps have become increasingly popular, users often find themselves trapped in a cycle of endless swiping, superficial interactions, and connections that rarely develop into lasting relationships.

Trova was created to address this growing challenge.

Founded with the belief that meaningful relationships should be built on compatibility, shared interests, and genuine intent, Trova is developing a dating platform designed to prioritize quality connections over the quantity of matches. The startup aims to create a more human centered dating experience where users can engage in authentic conversations and build relationships that extend beyond the digital world.

Unlike traditional dating platforms that emphasize rapid matching and appearance driven interactions, Trova focuses on fostering deeper connections between individuals who share similar values, interests, and relationship goals. The platform is designed to encourage intentional engagement, helping users move beyond casual interactions toward more meaningful relationships.

Starting in Abeokuta, Trova is currently building its early community while refining its product through user feedback and real world testing. This stage allows the team to better understand user needs, improve the overall experience, and establish a trusted environment where people can connect safely and confidently.

At its core, Trova is committed to making online dating more rewarding by creating a space where friendships, relationships, and long term partnerships can naturally develop. The startup believes that technology should not only connect people but also help them form genuine human relationships.

Looking ahead, Trova plans to expand beyond Abeokuta and reach users across Nigeria and beyond. Its long term vision is to become a trusted platform where meaningful connections flourish, redefining how relationships begin in the digital age.

As the dating landscape continues to evolve, Trova is positioning itself as a platform that values authenticity over algorithms and connection over convenience.

title: Inside Ogun State’s First Real Bet on Rural Tech Talent
excerpt: N.E.Y.I Techpreneurship Hub is opening new pathways into Nigeria’s digital economy for rural and semi-urban entrepreneurs in Ogun State, combining structured training, incubation, and mentorship to turn local talent into tech-ready founders.
body:
In 2012, Adefisoye Adeshola Joseph was a student at Moshood Abiola Polytechnic with a simple observation. Nobody was selling noodles and eggs at the school gate, and students were hungry for it. He started the business himself, then hired classmates to help him keep up with demand.

It wasn’t a tech idea. But it taught him something he’d build a career on: find the gap, build something to fill it, then bring others along.

More than a decade later, that lesson has grown into N.E.Y.I Techpreneurship Hub, based in Araromi, Abeokuta, right across from the polytechnic where it all started.

The gap N.E.Y.I is closing is bigger than noodles. Ogun State has a dense cluster of universities and polytechnics, but a large share of graduates leave school without the digital skills or industry exposure needed to work in Nigeria’s tech economy. N.E.Y.I exists to change that, specifically for people in rural and semi-urban areas who are usually left out of innovation hub conversations entirely.

What sets it apart is the structure. Instead of running one-off training sessions, N.E.Y.I moves participants through six stages: Discover, Train, Incubate, Attach, Launch, and Mentor. People come in learning digital marketing, prompt engineering, and AI tools, then get connected to real opportunities, incubation support, and mentorship as they build their own ventures.

The numbers suggest the model is working. N.E.Y.I has built a network of over 20,000 entrepreneurs and young people, trained more than 6,000, supported over 5,000 startups, and incubated more than 500 ventures. The hub also runs community programs like Scoutpreneurship in Tech and Kidpreneurship in Tech, aimed at introducing tech skills earlier and more broadly.

In 2024, the Tony Elumelu Foundation backed the hub with funding that let it acquire a permanent site in Araromi. That space is now being expanded into a larger co-working and innovation campus.

The recognition has followed. N.E.Y.I was selected by the Office for Nigerian Digital Innovation, under NITDA and the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, as the iHatch Innovation Hub for Ogun State’s fifth cohort. It has also been recognized by the Industrial Training Fund, Junior Chamber International, and the Ogun Tech Community.

Adefisoye’s plan now is to turn N.E.Y.I into a model other rural innovation hubs across Nigeria and Africa can follow. For a hub built on the idea that geography shouldn’t decide who gets access to opportunity, that ambition tracks.

title: TRAX Positions Itself as an Ecosystem Storytelling Platform for Ogun State Tech Scene
excerpt: TRAX defines itself as a Pan-African tech media and ecosystem intelligence platform focused on documenting Ogun State’s innovation landscape through structured storytelling, startup visibility, and curated ecosystem updates across founders, communities, and events.
body:
TRAX is being positioned as a structured media and ecosystem storytelling platform focused on documenting and amplifying the technology ecosystem in Ogun State, Nigeria. The platform centers on making local innovation visible through curated reporting on startups, founders, and community-driven developments.

Rather than functioning as a conventional news dashboard or blog,TRAX is designed as a hybrid system combining elements of tech media, startup directory, and ecosystem intelligence tooling. Its core focus is to organize and present information about Ogun State’s growing technology landscape in a structured and consistent format.
At the center of its identity is a narrative principle that stories which are not documented risk becoming invisible. In this framing, TRAX positions itself as a platform dedicated to ensuring that local innovation is recorded, structured, and made accessible through ongoing storytelling.
The platform’s content direction spans startups, tech communities, events, and ecosystem updates. Instead of treating these as isolated news items, TRAX organizes them as part of a broader ecosystem record, aimed at showing how innovation develops across the region over time.
Its design and product philosophy emphasize structure and consistency. TRAX is described as a system built around repeatable rules for branding, editorial tone, and visual identity, allowing it to function not only as a publication but also as a scalable framework for documenting ecosystem activity.

Within the broader Nigerian technology landscape, TRAX reflects a growing shift toward region-specific digital media platforms that focus on structured ecosystem mapping rather than general tech news coverage. Its emphasis on Ogun State highlights the increasing decentralization of tech storytelling beyond Nigeria’s primary hubs.
This approach aligns with a wider trend in emerging tech ecosystems where visibility, documentation, and narrative infrastructure are becoming key components of growth and investment attraction.
As regional innovation ecosystems continue to expand, platforms like TRAX illustrate a move toward more structured and deliberate documentation of local technology activity, positioning storytelling itself as a foundational layer of ecosystem development.

title: How OgunLearn Is Powering a New Era of Digital Education in Nigeria
excerpt: Ogun State's AI-powered OgunLearn platform is advancing digital education through smart learning tools, real-time performance tracking, and a student identification framework that is now influencing education reforms across Nigeria.
body:
The adoption of digital technology in Nigeria's education sector continues to gain momentum, with Ogun State emerging as one of the country's most active testing grounds for innovation in teaching and learning.
Recent recognition of top-performing educators on the OgunLearn platform has drawn renewed attention to the state's efforts to integrate artificial intelligence and data-driven systems into public education. At a ceremony held at the June 12 Cultural Centre in Abeokuta, the Ogun State Ministry of Education honoured 10 teachers who demonstrated exceptional use of the platform, rewarding them with tablet devices to support continued digital instruction.
OgunLearn was introduced as an AI-powered learning platform designed to help schools modernize classroom delivery and educational management. Through its integrated Learning Management System (LMS), teachers can access curriculum-aligned lesson notes, administer quizzes, manage digital gradebooks, and deliver more interactive learning experiences.
Beyond providing digital teaching resources, the platform incorporates performance analytics that enable educators to monitor student progress in real time. Teachers can identify learning gaps, track strengths and weaknesses, and make more informed instructional decisions using data generated through the system.
A key component of the initiative is the Learner Identification Number (LIN), a student-tracking framework developed by the Ogun State Ministry of Education. The system assigns learners a unique identity throughout their educational journey, helping improve record management, reduce examination irregularities, and support evidence-based educational planning.
The impact of the framework has extended beyond the state level. The Federal Government has adopted a similar model known as the Examination Learner Identification Number (ELIN), which is intended to strengthen student records management, improve assessment processes, and address challenges associated with entrance examinations nationwide.
The development reflects a broader shift toward technology-enabled education across Nigeria, where governments and institutions are increasingly exploring digital tools to improve learning outcomes and administrative efficiency.
As adoption of platforms like OgunLearn expands, Ogun State's approach may offer a glimpse into how artificial intelligence, digital identity systems, and data analytics could shape the future of public education across the country.

title: Multi Graphix INC: Helping Businesses Stand Out Through Design and Web Development

body:
Multi Graphix INC is a graphic design and web development startup dedicated to helping businesses overcome the challenges of poor visual branding and limited online visibility.

The company provides creative design solutions and professional website development services that enable businesses to present themselves more effectively, attract customers, and grow their digital presence.

By combining creativity with technology, Multi Graphix INC supports organizations in building strong brands and modern websites that reflect their goals and values.

title: Ogun Tech Community Concludes AI and Data Solutions Workshop Series Across Crescent and Chrisland Universities
excerpt: The Ogun Tech Community (OTC) has completed a two day workshop series focused on data engineering, analytics, and artificial intelligence, equipping students at Crescent University and Chrisland University with practical industry skills using Microsoft Fabric.
body:
The Ogun Tech Community (OTC) has successfully concluded a collaborative workshop series aimed at bridging the gap between academic learning and the rapidly evolving technology industry.

Titled "Building AI Driven Data Solutions with Microsoft Fabric," the initiative brought together students, technology enthusiasts, and aspiring professionals for hands on learning in modern data engineering, analytics, and artificial intelligence. The workshop was facilitated by Data Engineer Akpan Samuel, who guided participants through practical applications of enterprise grade data technologies.

The first session was held at the ICT Laboratory of Crescent University, Abeokuta, in collaboration with the College of Information and Communication Technology. Participants were introduced to the fundamentals of data engineering, including data pipelines, database architecture, and preparing datasets for artificial intelligence and machine learning applications.

The second session took place at the Department of Computer Science Laboratory, Chrisland University. Building on the foundation established during the first day, participants explored real time data processing, dashboard development, analytics workflows, and AI deployment using structured data platforms.

Throughout the workshop, attendees gained practical exposure to four key areas: Artificial Intelligence, Data Engineering, Data Analytics, and Microsoft Fabric. Through demonstrations, coding exercises, and collaborative activities, participants learned how modern organizations transform data into actionable insights and intelligent solutions.

Speaking during the workshop, facilitator Akpan Samuel emphasized the importance of strong data infrastructure in building effective AI systems. He noted that while artificial intelligence continues to grow rapidly, reliable and well structured data remains the foundation that powers successful AI applications.

The workshop concluded with interactive discussions, networking opportunities, and collaborative learning sessions. Through initiatives like this, the Ogun Tech Community continues to strengthen Ogun State's technology ecosystem by providing students with access to industry relevant knowledge and practical experience.
